key_insight: EHRAdapt lets frozen language models work directly with EHR event tuples by combining a clinical semantic prior with a learned evidence residual, which helps especially for rare events.
clinical_relevance: This could improve EHR-based prediction and downstream disease classification by preserving clinical meaning without inflating records into long text sequences.
method: Encodes each EHR event as (time, modality, code) instead of serializing it as text.
Adds modality embeddings and time-gap attention biases while mapping event codes into the model's input space.
Represents each code with a frozen ontology-based semantic prior plus a learned low-rank residual that grows with evidence.
evidence_signal: The adapter was continued-pretrained on records from about 4 million patients and evaluated with held-out next-event prediction and downstream infectious-disease/syndromic classification across three frozen backbones.
watch_item: Rare-event gains depend on ontology descriptions and projection quality, so performance may vary when code semantics are sparse or local coding systems differ.
paper_title: EHRAdapt: Adapting Pretrained Language Models to Electronic Health Records with Semantic Priors for Rare Clinical Events
